markets: Global: New York, London, Milan, Paris and Copenhagen runways; applies to premium and mid-market womenswear
title: SS27 Women's Season Colours
summary: Lilac and violet lead the womenswear palette, with butter for softness and true red and Klein blue for statement pieces. White is the neutral that is rising; warm browns and greys give way.

sections.heading: The palette
sections.body:
| Colour | Pantone TCX (nearest) | HEX | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lilac | 15-3720 TCX | #B3A0C9 | Seasonal: lead colour |
| Violet | 19-3642 TCX | #603F83 | Seasonal: depth and evening |
| Butter | 12-0711 TCX | #F6E199 | Seasonal: soft neutral |
| True red | 18-1763 TCX | #C71F2D | Seasonal: statement |
| Klein blue | 18-3949 TCX | #3850A0 | Accent: statement |
| Optic white | 11-0602 TCX | #F2F0EB | Core |

These colours come from Forecut's SS27 colour forecast, built from runway colour shares, editorial colour reports and Première Vision's key colours<sup>[1]</sup>. Pantone TCX codes are the nearest published match: confirm against a physical Pantone book before dyeing.

sections.heading: The evidence
sections.body:
**Purple is the season's new colour.** Chanel showed lilac, Miu Miu royal purple, and violet ran through Milan<sup>[2]</sup>.

**Soft, calming pastels.** Pascal K. Douglas described "colours that soothe and lower cortisol levels: butter, lavender, sage"<sup>[3]</sup>. Victoria Beckham and Icicle in Paris and Ashley Williams in London showed shoulder-padded shirts in light blue, yellow and baby pink; Bottega Veneta paired light-yellow pleated trousers with a bright pink jabot blouse<sup>[3]</sup>. Dior used a ballet-slipper pink across blazers, skirts and dresses<sup>[4]</sup>.

**Strong blocks of primary colour.** Chanel, Balenciaga and Celine paired canary yellow, true red and cobalt in strong blocks<sup>[2]</sup>.

**White up, browns down.** White rose from 23.7% to 28.4% of looks and ecru gained 1.4 points, while chocolate, almond and grey each lost between 1.5 and 1.8 points<sup>[5]</sup>. Black remains the most worn colour at 35.2%<sup>[5]</sup>.

**Gold as a full look.** At Saint Laurent, 49 of 59 looks were gold, from brass to rose<sup>[4]</sup>. Treat gold as a finish (lamé, metallic thread, hardware) rather than a dyed colour.

sections.heading: Colour groups and how much to use
sections.body:
- **Core (about half the range):** optic white and black, with sand and midnight from the season's shared key colours for depth.
- **Seasonal (about a third):** lilac, violet, butter and true red. Lilac and butter carry day pieces; violet and red carry evening and statement pieces.
- **Accent (the rest):** Klein blue, and gold as a finish. One piece or one detail per look.

sections.heading: Combinations and applications
sections.body:
- **Lilac with butter and white.** The softest combination: shirts, knitwear and skirts for day.
- **Violet with true red.** An evening and occasion pairing; use satin or duchesse to carry the depth.
- **Head-to-toe single colour.** Céline, Akris and Stella McCartney showed one shade from head to toe <sup>[2]</sup>; lilac, red or white work best.
- **Primary blocks.** True red, Klein blue and butter in large, flat blocks on tailoring and knitwear.
- **White as the base.** Optic white suits, skirts and shirts take any of the seasonal colours as an accent.

timing: Lilac and violet are rising into SS27 and continue into winter: Première Vision's AW27-28 trend forum opened with deep violet, plums, dusty pinks and mauves <sup>[6]</sup>. Butter and pastels are a summer story. White is rising for SS27; warm browns are fading.
products:
- **Lilac and butter:** shirts, knitwear, skirts, summer tailoring.
- **Violet and true red:** occasion dresses, satin skirts, statement tailoring.
- **Klein blue:** knitwear, shirts, accessories.
- **Optic white:** suiting, shirting, layered summer dresses.
design_implications:
- **Approve one standard per colour.** Head-to-toe and colour-blocked looks need every fabric and trim to match one approved shade; each white needs its own standard.
- **Test lilac across fibres.** Lilac shifts strongly between silk, cotton and polyester; dye lab dips on every base cloth.
- **Use gold as a finish.** Lamé, metallic yarns and hardware, not a dyed colour.
commercial_implications:
- **Lead with lilac in visual merchandising** and keep it in depth across categories, so a customer can build a full look.
- **Buy red and Klein blue lighter.** Strong colours sell as statements: fewer units, more styles.
- **Reduce warm browns** compared with AW26 and SS26 buys; move the neutral budget towards white and ecru.
